intent.raw_query: Hawaii family beach vacation, $5000, 10 days, August 2026 from Seattle

selected_hotel.name: Hanauma Bay, East Oahu Boutique Stay

experiences.name: Snorkeling at Hanauma Bay Nature Preserve
experiences.description: A world-renowned snorkeling spot set in a volcanic crater bay, perfect for families to explore vibrant coral reefs and tropical fish in calm, shallow waters. Kids and adults alike will be amazed by the marine life. Entry requires advance online reservations.

experiences.name: Polynesian Cultural Center
experiences.description: An immersive cultural theme park where families can explore six authentic Polynesian villages representing Hawaii, Samoa, Tonga, Fiji, Tahiti, and New Zealand. Includes live demonstrations, canoe rides, and a spectacular evening luau show that brings Pacific Island traditions to life.

experiences.name: Waimea Valley Botanical Garden and Waterfall Hike
experiences.description: A family-friendly guided walk through lush tropical botanical gardens leading to the stunning 45-foot Waimea Falls. Kids can swim in the natural pool at the base of the waterfall (life jackets provided). The valley is also rich in Hawaiian cultural history with on-site demonstrations.

experiences.name: Kaanapali Beach Family Day
experiences.description: Spend a full day at one of Hawaii's most beautiful and family-friendly beaches on Maui. Build sandcastles, bodyboard gentle waves, and snorkel around Black Rock (Pu'u Keka'a) where sea turtles and tropical fish are commonly spotted. Beach equipment rentals are affordable and widely available along the shore.

experiences.name: Hawaii Volcanoes National Park Exploration
experiences.description: Explore the awe-inspiring volcanic landscapes of the Big Island, including the Kilauea caldera, lava tube caves, and unique black lava fields. The park offers ranger-led family programs, easy crater rim walks, and the chance to see active volcanic activity. An unforgettable educational adventure for children and adults.
experiences.location: Hawaii Volcanoes National Park, Big Island

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Hawaii
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled — flight arrives at 13:00. Rest and travel time.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Daniel K. Inouye International Airport at 13:00. Collect luggage, pick up a rental car or take TheBus Route 23 toward East Oahu. Check in to the Hanauma Bay Boutique Stay (~45 min from airport). Freshen up, unpack, and get oriented with your surroundings.
day_by_day.evening: Take a short stroll along the coast near Hanauma Bay to enjoy the sunset views. Visit the Koko Marina Center nearby for a relaxed first dinner and to pick up groceries at Times Supermarket for budget breakfasts and snacks throughout the trip.

meals.breakfast: N/A — in transit
meals.lunch: Grab a quick bite at the airport — L&L Hawaiian Barbecue in the terminal offers affordable plate lunches (~$10–$13 per person)
meals.dinner: Koko Marina Center: Zippy's Restaurant — a beloved local chain with hearty, affordable Hawaiian comfort food (chili, saimin, plate lunches ~$10–$14 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Stop at Times Supermarket in Koko Marina to stock up on breakfast items (fruit, cereal, yogurt, juice) and snacks to save money throughout the trip. Budget tip: TheBus is only $3/ride but a rental car gives more flexibility for East Oahu and Big Island day trips.

day_by_day.morning: Early morning visit to Hanauma Bay Nature Preserve — one of Hawaii's top snorkeling spots, just minutes from your hotel. Arrive by 7:00–7:30 AM to beat crowds and secure entry (reservations required in advance at hanauma bay.org; entry fee ~$25/adult, children under 12 free). Watch the mandatory marine education video, then snorkel the crystal-clear reef teeming with sea turtles and tropical fish.
day_by_day.afternoon: Drive the scenic Kalanianaole Highway (Hwy 72) along the southeastern coast. Stop at Halona Blowhole Lookout (free), Sandy Beach Park for boogie boarding and people-watching (free), and Makapuu Point Lighthouse Trail (free, ~2 miles round trip) for stunning ocean views and possible whale or sea turtle sightings.
day_by_day.evening: Head to nearby Kaimana Beach (Sans Souci Beach) in Waikiki for a relaxed sunset swim. Browse the Waikiki area and grab dinner at a local spot before heading back to East Oahu.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered at the hotel — fruit, cereal, or yogurt from yesterday's grocery run
meals.lunch: Pack a picnic lunch from grocery store items (sandwiches, chips, fruit) to enjoy at Sandy Beach Park — saves $15–$20 per person
meals.dinner: Rainbow Drive-In (Kapahulu Ave, Honolulu) — iconic local plate lunch spot, open late; mixed plate with two scoops rice and mac salad ~$10–$12

day_by_day.notes: Book Hanauma Bay reservations well in advance — they sell out fast, especially in summer. Bring reef-safe sunscreen (required), snorkel gear (rentable on-site ~$15 or buy at Walmart for ~$20 to use all trip), and water shoes. Parking at Hanauma Bay is $3.

day_by_day.morning: Drive to Kailua Beach Park on the Windward Coast (~25 min from hotel) — consistently rated one of the best beaches in the US. Enjoy the calm, turquoise waters perfect for families. Rent kayaks or stand-up paddleboards from Kailua Beach Adventures (~$30–$40/hour for a double kayak) and paddle to the nearby Mokulua Islands (Mokes).
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the charming Kailua Town. Browse local boutiques and visit Kalapawai Market for a snack. Drive to Lanikai Beach (~5 min from Kailua) for more stunning scenery and calm swimming. Hike the short Lanikai Pillbox Trail (Kaiwa Ridge Trail, ~1.8 miles round trip, free) for panoramic views of the Mokulua Islands and Windward Coast.
day_by_day.evening: Return toward East Oahu. Stop at Waimanalo Beach on the way back for a golden-hour walk on one of Oahu's longest stretches of white sand beach (free).

meals.breakfast: Self-catered at hotel
meals.lunch: Kalapawai Market & Deli in Kailua — fresh sandwiches, wraps, and local snacks (~$10–$14). Eat on the beach!
meals.dinner: Ono Seafood (Honolulu) — famous for fresh poke bowls at very reasonable prices (~$12–$16). Take it to go and enjoy at home or a nearby park.

day_by_day.notes: Kailua Beach parking is free and plentiful. The Pillbox hike is moderately easy but can be hot — go in the late afternoon for cooler temps and better light. Bring plenty of water and sunscreen.

day_by_day.morning: Drive the scenic Pali Highway over the Ko'olau Mountains to the Nuuanu Pali Lookout (free, $3 parking) — a dramatic cliff with sweeping views of the Windward Coast and a fascinating Hawaiian history lesson about the Battle of Nu'uanu. Continue to the North Shore of Oahu (~45 min drive). Visit Waimea Bay Beach Park — calm and perfect for swimming in summer months.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the legendary North Shore surf town of Haleiwa. Walk the charming main street, visit local surf shops, and browse art galleries. Stop at Shark's Cove (Pupukea Beach Park) for excellent snorkeling in its natural lava rock pools (free). Visit Waimea Valley (entry ~$20/adult, $10 children) for a peaceful botanical garden walk leading to a beautiful freshwater waterfall you can swim in.
day_by_day.evening: Grab famous shave ice in Haleiwa before heading back south. Watch the sunset from Sunset Beach (free) on the way back.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered at hotel — eat before the drive
meals.lunch: Giovanni's Shrimp Truck (Haleiwa) — iconic North Shore food truck; scampi or spicy garlic shrimp plate with rice ~$14–$16
meals.dinner: Matsumoto Shave Ice for dessert (~$4–$6), then self-catered dinner at the hotel using grocery items to balance the budget

day_by_day.notes: North Shore is about 1 hour from East Oahu — plan for a full day. In summer, North Shore waves are small and safe for swimming. Winter (Nov–Feb) brings massive surf. Budget tip: Waimea Valley is worth the entry fee for families — kids love the waterfall swim.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Diamond Head State Monument (~15 min from hotel) — one of Hawaii's most iconic hikes. The 1.6-mile round-trip trail leads to the summit of the famous volcanic crater with 360-degree views of Honolulu and the Pacific Ocean. Entry: $5/person or $10/car. Arrive early (opens at 6:00 AM) to beat the heat and crowds.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Waikiki Beach for the afternoon — enjoy the famous stretch of beach, swim in the warm surf, and watch outrigger canoe clubs practice. Visit Kapiolani Park (free) adjacent to Waikiki for a relaxed picnic. Walk through the Honolulu Zoo entrance area and enjoy the free Waikiki Aquarium exterior gardens. Explore Kalakaua Avenue for window shopping.
day_by_day.evening: Attend a free Friday Night Fireworks show preview at Hilton Hawaiian Village (actually on Fridays, so note this is Thursday — instead enjoy a free sunset hula show at Kuhio Beach Hula Mound at 6:30 PM and 7:30 PM, free!). Stroll the Waikiki waterfront at night.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered at hotel before the Diamond Head hike
meals.lunch: Waikiki: Marukame Udon (Kuhio Ave) — one of the best budget eats in Waikiki; fresh udon noodles from ~$5–$9, add tempura for ~$1–$2 each. Expect a line but it moves fast!
meals.dinner: Ono Hawaiian Foods (Kapahulu Ave) — authentic Hawaiian food: laulau, poi, kalua pig, haupia ~$12–$16. A true local institution.

day_by_day.notes: Diamond Head trail is paved but steep in sections with stairs and a tunnel — manageable for most families. Bring water and wear good shoes. Book Diamond Head entry online in advance (gostateparks.hawaii.gov). The free Kuhio Beach hula show is a wonderful cultural experience — arrive 15 min early for good viewing spots.

day_by_day.morning: Explore downtown Honolulu's historic and cultural sites — all very affordable or free. Visit Iolani Palace ($22/adult, $6 children — the only royal palace on US soil), the King Kamehameha Statue (free), and Kawaiahao Church (free). Walk through Chinatown for a fascinating cultural experience and browse the Oahu Market and local herb shops.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Bishop Museum (~$25/adult, $16 children) — Hawaii's premier natural history and cultural museum with incredible Hawaiian artifacts, a planetarium, and Science Adventure Center. Perfect for families and very educational. Alternatively, save money and visit the free Hawaii State Art Museum (HISAM) in downtown Honolulu.
day_by_day.evening: It's Friday! Head to the Hilton Hawaiian Village on Waikiki Beach for the FREE Friday Night Fireworks show at approximately 7:45 PM — a spectacular weekly tradition. Watch from the beach for the best free view. Enjoy the festive atmosphere of Waikiki on a Friday night.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered at hotel
meals.lunch: Chinatown, Honolulu: Duc's Bistro or Fook Yuen Seafood Restaurant — authentic Asian cuisine with generous portions at low prices (~$8–$13). Or grab dim sum from a local bakery for ~$5.
meals.dinner: Pre-fireworks: grab plate lunches or poke bowls from Foodland Farms (Ala Moana) or a food truck near Waikiki — budget ~$10–$14. Enjoy dinner on the beach while waiting for fireworks!

day_by_day.notes: The Bishop Museum is one of the best museums in the Pacific — highly recommended for families interested in Hawaiian culture and natural history. Friday fireworks are free but the beach gets crowded — arrive by 7:00 PM for a good spot. Budget tip: Avoid overpriced Waikiki restaurants tonight and use the food truck/grocery option.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Pearl Harbor National Memorial — one of the most significant historical sites in the US. The USS Arizona Memorial is free (timed-entry tickets required at recreation.gov, book weeks in advance). Arrive at the Pearl Harbor Visitor Center early (~8:00 AM). The boat tour to the memorial is free; allow 2–3 hours for the full experience.
day_by_day.afternoon: Add-on tours at Pearl Harbor if interested: USS Bowfin Submarine Museum (~$27/adult, $13 children) or USS Missouri Battleship (~$32/adult, $16 children) — choose one to manage budget. Alternatively, visit the free exhibits at the Visitor Center. Head to Ala Moana Beach Park (free) for a relaxing afternoon swim — a beautiful, less-touristy beach than Waikiki.
day_by_day.evening: Visit Ala Moana Center — Hawaii's largest open-air shopping mall — for window shopping and affordable dining options. Browse the food court for budget-friendly local options. Enjoy a Saturday evening stroll along Ala Moana Beach Park as the sun sets.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered at hotel — eat before the early Pearl Harbor departure
meals.lunch: Pack snacks and water for Pearl Harbor (no food inside memorial). Grab lunch afterward at Shiro's Saimin Haven (Aiea, near Pearl Harbor) — authentic local saimin noodle soup ~$8–$12
meals.dinner: Ala Moana Center Food Court: Panda Express, Manchu Wok, or local options like Goma Tei Ramen (~$10–$14). Or self-catered dinner at hotel.

day_by_day.notes: Pearl Harbor requires advance booking — do this NOW if not already done (recreation.gov). Free timed-entry tickets go fast, especially in summer. Children under 4 are not permitted on the USS Arizona Memorial boat tour. Ala Moana Beach Park is a locals' favorite — clean, calm, and free with parking.

day_by_day.morning: Today is a travel day to the Big Island! Take an inter-island flight from Honolulu (HNL) to Kona (KOA) or Hilo (ITO) — book in advance with Hawaiian Airlines or Southwest for ~$60–$120/person round trip. Morning flight recommended. If flying to Kona, rent a car at the airport and drive to Hawaii Volcanoes National Park (~2 hours). If flying to Hilo, the park is only ~45 min away.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Hawaii Volcanoes National Park (entry $35/vehicle, valid for 7 days — great value!). Begin exploring: visit the Kilauea Visitor Center to get oriented and check current volcanic activity. Walk the Crater Rim Trail and stop at the Kilauea Overlook for dramatic views of the caldera. Visit the Sulphur Banks (Ha'akulamanu) Trail (~1.2 miles, easy, free with park entry).
day_by_day.evening: As darkness falls, the lava glow from Kilauea becomes most spectacular. Return to the Kilauea Overlook or Jaggar Museum Overlook area for stunning nighttime views of the glowing caldera — one of the most unforgettable natural experiences in Hawaii. Drive back to Hilo or Kona for overnight accommodation.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered at East Oahu hotel before airport departure
meals.lunch: Pack snacks for the flight and drive. Or grab a quick bite in Hilo: Ken's House of Pancakes (open 24/7) — generous portions at great prices (~$10–$14)
meals.dinner: Hilo: Cafe 100 — famous for their Loco Moco (a Hawaiian staple: rice, hamburger patty, fried egg, gravy) from ~$5–$9. One of the most affordable and authentic local meals in Hawaii!

day_by_day.notes: Book inter-island flights well in advance for the best prices. Check volcanic activity status at nps.gov/havo before visiting — lava viewing conditions change frequently. The park is open 24/7, making evening visits possible and magical. Budget accommodation in Hilo: Hilo Bay Hostel (~$35–$50/night) or budget motels near the park.

day_by_day.morning: Full day at Hawaii Volcanoes National Park. Start early with the Chain of Craters Road — a dramatic 19-mile road descending 3,700 feet through ancient lava flows to the coast. Stop at Holei Sea Arch (free with park entry) and walk the Pu'u Loa Petroglyphs Trail (~1.4 miles round trip) to see over 23,000 ancient Hawaiian rock carvings — one of the largest petroglyph fields in Hawaii.
day_by_day.afternoon: Hike the Kilauea Iki Trail (~4 miles, moderate, 2–3 hours) — a spectacular loop descending into a solidified lava lake that erupted in 1959. Walk across the crater floor surrounded by steaming vents — an otherworldly experience perfect for families (older children). Visit the Thurston Lava Tube (Nahuku) — a 500-year-old lava tube you can walk through (~0.3 miles, easy, free with park entry).
day_by_day.evening: Drive to the Punaluu Black Sand Beach (~45 min from the park) — one of Hawaii's most unique beaches with jet-black volcanic sand. Hawaiian green sea turtles (honu) frequently rest on the beach — a magical wildlife encounter. Watch the sunset over the black sand before returning to your accommodation.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered or Ken's House of Pancakes in Hilo for a hearty breakfast before a full hiking day
meals.lunch: Pack a picnic lunch from the grocery store — eat at one of the park's scenic overlooks or picnic areas. Volcano House Restaurant inside the park has great views but is pricier (~$18–$25 entrees).
meals.dinner: Hilo: Suisan Fish Market — fresh local poke and seafood at market prices (~$12–$16 for a generous poke bowl). A true local experience.

day_by_day.notes: Wear sturdy closed-toe shoes for lava field hiking — the terrain is sharp and uneven. Bring plenty of water (2+ liters per person), sunscreen, and layers (the park can be cool and misty). At Punaluu, do NOT touch or disturb the sea turtles — it is illegal and they need their rest. This is one of the most memorable days of the entire trip!

day_by_day.morning: Final morning on the Big Island. If flying from Kona, drive up to the Kona Coffee Living History Farm or browse the Kona Coffee Belt along Highway 11 for free scenic views and free tastings at small family farms. Visit Magic Sand Beach (La'aloa Beach) in Kailua-Kona — a beautiful white sand beach with good snorkeling. If flying from Hilo, visit Rainbow Falls (Waianuenue) — a stunning 80-foot waterfall just 2 miles from downtown Hilo (free!).
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to the airport for your inter-island return flight to Honolulu (HNL). Allow extra time for the drive and check-in. Upon returning to Oahu, transfer back to your East Oahu hotel. Spend the last afternoon at Hanauma Bay area — take a final walk along the coastline, visit Koko Head Crater viewpoint, or simply relax on the beach near your hotel.
day_by_day.evening: Final evening in Hawaii — return to a favorite restaurant from the trip for a celebratory dinner. Take a final sunset walk along the East Oahu coast near Hanauma Bay. Reflect on 10 incredible days and begin packing for departure.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered or Island Naturals Market & Deli in Hilo — organic and local food options, hot bar with affordable breakfast items (~$8–$12)
meals.lunch: Airport or on the go — pack snacks from the grocery store or grab a quick bite before the flight
meals.dinner: Koko Marina Center: Buho Cocina y Cantina for Mexican-inspired dishes with ocean views, or return to Zippy's for a budget-friendly final meal (~$10–$15). Toast to a wonderful Hawaii adventure!

day_by_day.notes: Budget summary tips for the full trip: Use TheBus where possible ($3/ride), buy a 7-day bus pass ($70) if staying on Oahu. Cook breakfasts and pack lunches daily to save $20–$30/day per family. Book all national park entries, Pearl Harbor, and Hanauma Bay in advance online. Inter-island flights booked 4–6 weeks ahead can be as low as $59 each way. Total estimated daily budget (excluding accommodation and flights): $60–$90/day for a family of 4 with smart meal planning.

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at 13:00 — no morning activities scheduled. Flight LH lands; clear customs, collect luggage, and arrange ground transportation to Hanauma Bay, East Oahu Boutique Stay (approx. 30–45 min drive from HNL).
day_by_day.afternoon: Check in to the boutique stay, freshen up, and take a leisurely stroll along the scenic coastal path near Hanauma Bay to get oriented. Enjoy the ocean views and decompress from travel. Pick up essentials at a nearby grocery or convenience store.
day_by_day.evening: Casual welcome dinner at a local restaurant near Hawaii Kai or Koko Head area to celebrate your arrival in Hawaii.

meals.breakfast: On the plane or at the airport upon arrival.
meals.lunch: Grab a quick bite at the airport or a nearby fast-casual spot like L&L Hawaiian Barbecue near the airport (~$10–15/person).
meals.dinner: Kona Brewing Company – Hawaii Kai: Relaxed waterfront brewpub with fresh fish tacos, burgers, and local craft beers. Family-friendly and mid-range (~$20–35/person).

day_by_day.notes: Do not schedule anything before 13:00. Reserve snorkeling gear rental for Hanauma Bay the following morning — book the timed entry reservation online tonight as slots fill quickly. Hanauma Bay requires advance reservations.

day_by_day.morning: Snorkeling at Hanauma Bay Nature Preserve: Arrive early (7:00–8:00 AM) for your pre-booked timed entry. Watch the mandatory marine education video, then spend 2–3 hours snorkeling the vibrant reef teeming with tropical fish and sea turtles. Rent snorkel gear on-site if needed (~$12/set). This world-renowned volcanic crater bay is steps from your hotel.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to the boutique stay to rinse off and relax. Head to nearby Sandy Beach Park (10 min drive) for bodyboarding and beach play — a local favorite with dramatic shore break. Supervise young children closely as waves can be strong.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the Hawaii Kai Town Center area for shopping and a casual dinner. Walk the Koko Marina waterfront.

meals.breakfast: Grab breakfast at the boutique stay or pick up pastries and fruit from a nearby café before heading to Hanauma Bay.
meals.lunch: Picnic lunch at Hanauma Bay or Sandy Beach — pack sandwiches and snacks from a grocery store to save money (~$5–10/person).
meals.dinner: Nico's at Pier 38 or Koko Head Café (East Oahu): Fresh local fish plates and Hawaiian-inspired brunch-style dinners. Mid-range (~$18–28/person).

day_by_day.notes: Hanauma Bay is closed on Tuesdays for reef restoration. Sunscreen must be reef-safe (required by Hawaii state law). Arrive at Hanauma Bay no later than 7:30 AM as the parking lot fills fast. Bring water shoes for rocky reef areas.

day_by_day.morning: Since Hanauma Bay is closed on Tuesdays, visit Waimea Valley Botanical Garden and Waterfall Hike on the North Shore (approx. 1 hr drive from East Oahu). Enjoy a guided family-friendly walk through 1,800 acres of lush tropical botanical gardens filled with native Hawaiian plants, peacocks, and cultural artifacts.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the Waimea Valley experience — reach the stunning 45-foot Waihi Falls waterfall at the trail's end and swim in the freshwater pool (lifeguards on duty). Explore the cultural demonstrations and archaeological sites within the valley.
day_by_day.evening: Drive along the scenic North Shore, stop at Sunset Beach or Waimea Bay for a golden-hour stroll, then head back toward East Oahu.

meals.breakfast: Morning café stop en route to North Shore — try Ted's Bakery near Sunset Beach for legendary cream pies and plate lunches (~$8–12/person).
meals.lunch: Giovanni's Shrimp Truck (Kahuku): Famous garlic butter or lemon pepper shrimp plates — a North Shore institution (~$15–18/person). Cash preferred.
meals.dinner: Back in East Oahu: Zippy's Restaurant — a beloved local chain with affordable Hawaiian comfort food like chili, saimin, and plate lunches (~$12–18/person).

day_by_day.notes: Waimea Valley admission: ~$20 adults, ~$10 children (3–12). Bring water shoes for the waterfall swimming area. The North Shore drive is beautiful — allow extra time for photo stops. Traffic can build on H-1 heading back in the evening.

day_by_day.morning: Polynesian Cultural Center (Laie, North Shore — 45 min from East Oahu): Arrive at opening (noon package or morning self-guided). Explore six authentic Polynesian villages representing Hawaii, Samoa, Aotearoa (New Zealand), Fiji, Tahiti, and Tonga. Participate in hands-on cultural activities like fire-making, coconut husking, and canoe paddling.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue exploring the Polynesian Cultural Center villages. Watch the afternoon canoe pageant on the lagoon — a spectacular free cultural show included with admission. Browse the marketplace and try authentic Polynesian foods.
day_by_day.evening: Stay for the world-famous 'Ha: Breath of Life' evening show — a breathtaking theatrical production with fire dancers, acrobatics, and traditional music. Book the buffet dinner package for a seamless experience.

meals.breakfast: Light breakfast at the boutique stay before departing.
meals.lunch: Gateway Buffet at the Polynesian Cultural Center — included in many admission packages, featuring Hawaiian and Polynesian dishes (~$25–35/person if added on).
meals.dinner: Ali'i Luau Buffet dinner package at the Polynesian Cultural Center before the evening show — traditional Hawaiian imu-roasted kalua pig, poi, haupia dessert (~$45–65/person, book in advance).

day_by_day.notes: Book Polynesian Cultural Center tickets in advance online — combo packages with the evening show and dinner offer the best value (~$80–120/person). The center is run by Brigham Young University–Hawaii and is family-friendly. Plan for a full day (10 AM–9:30 PM). Free parking available.

day_by_day.morning: Relaxed beach morning at Lanikai Beach (20 min from hotel) — one of Oahu's most beautiful and calm white-sand beaches with crystal-clear turquoise water, ideal for families. Swim, build sandcastles, and kayak to the Mokulua Islands (rentals available nearby, ~$30–40/2hrs).
day_by_day.afternoon: Drive to Kailua town for lunch and afternoon exploration. Browse the charming boutique shops along Kailua Road. Visit Kailua Beach Park — a wide, stunning beach perfect for swimming and paddleboarding.
day_by_day.evening: Return to East Oahu for a relaxed dinner and early evening. Enjoy a sunset from the hotel area or nearby Makapuu Lookout.

meals.breakfast: Cinnamon's Restaurant (Kailua): Famous for their guava chiffon pancakes and Portuguese sausage omelets — a local breakfast institution (~$14–20/person).
meals.lunch: Kalapawai Market & Deli (Kailua): Gourmet sandwiches, salads, and fresh local ingredients in a casual café setting (~$12–18/person).
meals.dinner: Plumeria Beach House at Kahala Hotel (splurge-worthy mid-range dinner): Fresh Hawaiian seafood and locally sourced dishes with beautiful garden views (~$30–50/person).

day_by_day.notes: Lanikai Beach has limited parking — arrive early or park on Mokulua Drive and walk. No lifeguards at Lanikai; conditions are generally calm but always supervise children. Kailua Beach has lifeguards on duty.

day_by_day.morning: Inter-island flight to Maui (Kahului Airport, OGG) — book a short 35-min flight with Hawaiian Airlines or Southwest (~$80–150/person round trip). Depart early morning to maximize your Maui day. Rent a car at Kahului Airport for the day.
day_by_day.afternoon: Kaanapali Beach Family Day: Drive to West Maui (45 min from airport) and spend the afternoon at Kaanapali Beach — one of Hawaii's most iconic and family-friendly beaches. Build sandcastles, snorkel around Black Rock (Pu'u Keka'a) where cliff divers perform, and enjoy the gentle waves. Beach chairs and umbrella rentals available.
day_by_day.evening: Watch the traditional cliff diving ceremony at Black Rock at sunset — a free, spectacular daily event. Then stroll the Kaanapali Beach Walk lined with shops and restaurants before heading back to the airport for your return flight to Oahu.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at the boutique stay or airport before departure.
meals.lunch: Hula Grill Kaanapali (on the beach): Open-air beachfront restaurant with fresh fish sandwiches, salads, and tropical cocktails. Family-friendly and mid-range (~$20–35/person).
meals.dinner: Grab dinner near Kaanapali before heading to the airport — Leilani's on the Beach: Fresh seafood, burgers, and pasta with stunning ocean views (~$25–40/person).

day_by_day.notes: This is a day-trip to Maui — book inter-island flights well in advance for best prices. Alternatively, consider a 2-night stay in Maui by adjusting the itinerary. Return flight should be booked for late evening (8–9 PM) to allow full beach time. Confirm car rental includes inter-island coverage.

day_by_day.morning: Recovery and relaxed morning at the boutique stay. Sleep in, enjoy a leisurely breakfast, and spend the morning at the hotel pool or nearby Hanauma Bay area beach for a casual swim. Optional: re-visit Hanauma Bay for a second snorkel session (book a new timed entry).
day_by_day.afternoon: Drive to Diamond Head State Monument (20 min from hotel) for a family hike up the iconic volcanic crater. The 1.6-mile round-trip trail offers panoramic views of Waikiki and the Pacific Ocean. Allow 1.5–2 hours total.
day_by_day.evening: Head into Waikiki for the evening — explore Kalakaua Avenue, browse the International Market Place, and enjoy the vibrant beach-town atmosphere.

meals.breakfast: Leisurely breakfast at the boutique stay or a nearby café — try Rainbow Drive-In (Kapahulu): Classic Hawaiian plate lunch spot open for breakfast, famous for their loco moco (~$10–15/person).
meals.lunch: Picnic lunch packed from a grocery store enjoyed at Diamond Head's summit viewpoint or base area.
meals.dinner: Duke's Waikiki (on the beach): Iconic Waikiki institution named after Duke Kahanamoku — fresh fish, Hawaiian-style ribs, and hula dancing. Great family atmosphere (~$25–40/person).

day_by_day.notes: Diamond Head: $5/person entry fee (paid online in advance). Opens at 6:00 AM; go early to beat the heat and crowds. The trail has some steep sections and a tunnel — bring water and wear closed-toe shoes. Children 5+ can manage the hike comfortably.

day_by_day.morning: Inter-island flight to the Big Island (Kona or Hilo Airport) — depart early morning. Rent a car at the airport. Drive to Hawaii Volcanoes National Park (45 min from Hilo Airport, or 2.5 hrs from Kona). Begin exploration at the Kilauea Visitor Center to get oriented and pick up maps.
day_by_day.afternoon: Hawaii Volcanoes National Park Exploration: Drive the 11-mile Crater Rim Drive, stopping at the Kilauea Overlook for dramatic caldera views, the steam vents, and the Thurston Lava Tube (a walk-through ancient lava tunnel). Hike the Devastation Trail (0.9 miles, easy) through a landscape transformed by past eruptions.
day_by_day.evening: As darkness falls, view the glowing lava lake at Kilauea caldera from the Jaggar Museum overlook area (conditions permitting) — one of Hawaii's most awe-inspiring experiences. Return to Hilo for the night or take an evening flight back to Oahu.

meals.breakfast: Early airport breakfast or pack snacks for the drive.
meals.lunch: Cafe Ono at the Volcano House Hotel (inside the national park): Casual café with sandwiches, soups, and local specials with crater views (~$15–22/person).
meals.dinner: Hilo Bay Café (if staying overnight) or Cafe Pesto: Fresh local seafood, pasta, and Hawaiian fusion in a relaxed setting (~$20–35/person). Alternatively, pack a dinner to enjoy at the park during lava viewing.

day_by_day.notes: Hawaii Volcanoes National Park entrance: $35/vehicle (valid 7 days). Check the USGS Hawaiian Volcano Observatory website for current eruption status before visiting. Volcanic fumes (vog) can be hazardous — bring masks for sensitive individuals and avoid if pregnant. This can be a day trip or an overnight on the Big Island.

day_by_day.morning: Return to Oahu (morning flight if overnighted on Big Island) or final full day on Oahu. Visit the USS Arizona Memorial and Pearl Harbor National Memorial (45 min from East Oahu) — a profound and educational experience for the whole family. Book timed entry tickets in advance (free, but required).
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Battleship Missouri Memorial and Pacific Aviation Museum at Pearl Harbor (additional tickets required, ~$25–30/person each). These immersive exhibits bring WWII history to life in a compelling way for families.
day_by_day.evening: Return to East Oahu for a final relaxing evening. Visit Makapuu Lookout for a spectacular sunset view over the windward coast, then enjoy a farewell dinner near the hotel.

meals.breakfast: Morning café near the hotel or a quick stop at Liliha Bakery (Honolulu) for their famous coco puffs and fresh pastries (~$8–12/person).
meals.lunch: Highway Inn (Kakaako): Authentic Hawaiian comfort food — kalua pig, laulau, poi, and haupia in a casual, beloved local setting (~$15–22/person).
meals.dinner: Roy's Hawaii Kai: Signature Hawaiian fusion cuisine by renowned chef Roy Yamaguchi — fresh island fish, macadamia-crusted preparations, and creative desserts. A special farewell dinner (~$40–60/person).

day_by_day.notes: Pearl Harbor timed entry reservations must be booked weeks in advance at recreation.gov — the USS Arizona Memorial boat tour fills up extremely fast. Allow 3–4 hours minimum for the full Pearl Harbor experience. The site is deeply moving; prepare children with age-appropriate context beforehand.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Hawaii — enjoy a slow, peaceful breakfast and take one last swim or snorkel at Hanauma Bay (open again on Tuesdays — wait, closed Tuesdays; go to nearby Koko Head Tide Pools or Halona Blowhole Lookout instead for a scenic farewell). Pack bags and check out of the boutique stay.
day_by_day.afternoon: Drive to Honolulu International Airport (HNL) — allow 45–60 minutes from East Oahu. Return rental car if applicable. Check in for your departing flight, browse duty-free shops, and pick up last-minute souvenirs like Kona coffee, macadamia nuts, and Hawaiian sea salt.
day_by_day.evening: Depart Hawaii with wonderful memories. Mahalo and aloha!

meals.breakfast: One last local breakfast — Morning Glass Coffee + Café (Manoa): Artisan coffee, açaí bowls, and fresh pastries in a charming neighborhood setting (~$12–18/person).
meals.lunch: Airport lunch at Makai Market Food Court (HNL) or grab a final plate lunch from L&L Hawaiian Barbecue for the road (~$12–16/person).
meals.dinner: In-flight meal or at your layover destination.

day_by_day.notes: Check out time is typically 11:00 AM — confirm with the boutique stay. Hanauma Bay is closed on Tuesdays, so plan the morning accordingly. Allow extra time at the airport for security — HNL can be busy in peak summer season. Purchase any perishable food souvenirs (like fresh pineapple) from approved agricultural inspection stands at the airport to comply with USDA regulations.

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

trip_options.title: Premium Hawaii Escape
trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

hotel.name: Hanauma Bay, East Oahu Boutique Stay

experiences.name: Snorkeling at Hanauma Bay Nature Preserve
experiences.description: A world-renowned snorkeling spot set in a volcanic crater bay, perfect for families to explore vibrant coral reefs and tropical fish in calm, shallow waters. Kids and adults alike will be amazed by the marine life. Entry requires advance online reservations.

experiences.name: Polynesian Cultural Center
experiences.description: An immersive cultural theme park where families can explore six authentic Polynesian villages representing Hawaii, Samoa, Tonga, Fiji, Tahiti, and New Zealand. Includes live demonstrations, canoe rides, and a spectacular evening luau show that brings Pacific Island traditions to life.

experiences.name: Waimea Valley Botanical Garden and Waterfall Hike
experiences.description: A family-friendly guided walk through lush tropical botanical gardens leading to the stunning 45-foot Waimea Falls. Kids can swim in the natural pool at the base of the waterfall (life jackets provided). The valley is also rich in Hawaiian cultural history with on-site demonstrations.

experiences.name: Kaanapali Beach Family Day
experiences.description: Spend a full day at one of Hawaii's most beautiful and family-friendly beaches on Maui. Build sandcastles, bodyboard gentle waves, and snorkel around Black Rock (Pu'u Keka'a) where sea turtles and tropical fish are commonly spotted. Beach equipment rentals are affordable and widely available along the shore.

experiences.name: Hawaii Volcanoes National Park Exploration
experiences.description: Explore the awe-inspiring volcanic landscapes of the Big Island, including the Kilauea caldera, lava tube caves, and unique black lava fields. The park offers ranger-led family programs, easy crater rim walks, and the chance to see active volcanic activity. An unforgettable educational adventure for children and adults.
experiences.location: Hawaii Volcanoes National Park, Big Island

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at Honolulu International Airport at 13:00 — no morning activities scheduled. Private luxury transfer arranged from airport to Hanauma Bay, East Oahu Boutique Stay.
day_by_day.afternoon: Check in to the boutique property and settle into your suite. Take a leisurely stroll along the shoreline near Hanauma Bay to get your first taste of the stunning East Oahu coastline. Enjoy complimentary welcome refreshments and a private orientation with the concierge to review the week ahead.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset cocktails on the hotel terrace overlooking the Pacific, followed by a relaxed first dinner at the resort or a nearby acclaimed restaurant to recover from travel.

meals.breakfast: Enjoy snacks or a meal on the flight — nothing scheduled pre-arrival.
meals.lunch: Light welcome spread arranged by the hotel upon check-in: fresh tropical fruit, local cheeses, and sparkling water.
meals.dinner: Dinner at 3660 on the Rise (Kaimuki, ~15 min drive) — an upscale Euro-Island fusion restaurant celebrated for fresh local seafood and an extensive wine list.

day_by_day.notes: Keep Day 1 light to allow the family to rest and adjust to the Hawaii Standard Time zone (HST, UTC-10). Confirm all upcoming reservations with the concierge this evening.

day_by_day.morning: Snorkeling at Hanauma Bay Nature Preserve — just minutes from the hotel, this is the perfect first full-day activity. Arrive early (pre-booked private guided session at 8:00 AM) to enjoy the bay before crowds build. A certified marine naturalist will guide the family through the vibrant coral reef ecosystem inside the volcanic crater bay.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to the hotel for a poolside lunch and rest. In the mid-afternoon, take a scenic drive along the Kalanianaole Highway to Makapuu Point Lighthouse Trail for panoramic ocean views — a gentle 2-mile paved walk suitable for all ages, with possible humpback whale sightings (August season note: look for spinner dolphins instead).
day_by_day.evening: Sunset at Makapuu Beach Park, then head to a fine dining dinner in Honolulu.

meals.breakfast: Gourmet in-room breakfast delivered by the hotel — fresh acai bowls, eggs Benedict with loco moco twist, Kona coffee, and fresh-squeezed lilikoi juice.
meals.lunch: Poolside lunch at the hotel — grilled mahi-mahi tacos, poke bowls, and tropical smoothies.
meals.dinner: Nobu Honolulu (Waikiki, ~20 min drive) — world-class Japanese-Peruvian cuisine with premium omakase options, ideal for a luxurious family evening.

day_by_day.notes: Hanauma Bay requires advance reservations and charges a conservation fee. The private guided snorkel session should be pre-booked through the concierge. Apply reef-safe sunscreen only — the preserve strictly enforces this.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Polynesian Cultural Center in Laie (approximately 45 minutes north of the hotel via H-3 and Kamehameha Highway). Arrive at opening (9:00 AM) for a full immersive experience exploring six authentic Polynesian villages — Hawaii, Samoa, Aotearoa, Fiji, Tahiti, and Tonga. Enjoy live cultural demonstrations, canoe rides, and hands-on activities perfect for the whole family.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue exploring the Polynesian Cultural Center — attend the spectacular 'Ha: Breath of Life' afternoon show rehearsal viewing (if available) or participate in the premium Ambassador Dining experience. Explore the IMAX theater and interactive exhibits.
day_by_day.evening: Stay for the renowned 'Ha: Breath of Life' evening luau and fire-knife dance spectacular — one of Hawaii's most celebrated cultural performances. VIP seating and premium dinner package included.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the hotel before departure — continental spread with Hawaiian sweet bread French toast, tropical fruit platter, and Kona coffee.
meals.lunch: Ali'i Luau Luncheon at the Polynesian Cultural Center — an all-you-can-eat premium buffet featuring kalua pork, poi, haupia, and island-style sides.
meals.dinner: Ha: Breath of Life VIP Dinner Package at the Polynesian Cultural Center — premium luau feast with reserved seating for the evening show.

day_by_day.notes: Book VIP packages for the Polynesian Cultural Center well in advance — they sell out quickly, especially in August. The full day experience (9 AM to 9:30 PM) is long; bring comfortable shoes and light layers for the evening show. Consider hiring a private driver for the day to avoid parking stress.

day_by_day.morning: Private catamaran sailing charter departing from Kewalo Basin Harbor (20 min from hotel). Enjoy a 3-hour luxury sail along the Oahu coastline with a private crew, onboard snorkeling, and a gourmet continental breakfast served at sea. Spot sea turtles, tropical fish, and possibly spinner dolphins.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to East Oahu and spend the afternoon at Lanikai Beach — one of Hawaii's most pristine and picturesque stretches of white sand, just 15 minutes from the hotel. Rent premium beach chairs, umbrellas, and paddleboards through the hotel concierge for a relaxed family beach afternoon.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset kayaking to the Mokulua Islands (the twin islets off Lanikai Beach) with a private guide, followed by a beachside dinner experience.

meals.breakfast: Gourmet continental breakfast served aboard the private catamaran — smoked salmon bagels, fresh pastries, tropical fruit, mimosas (adults), and fresh juice (children).
meals.lunch: Picnic-style beach lunch delivered by the hotel — premium bento boxes with poke, sushi rolls, edamame, and sparkling water, enjoyed on Lanikai Beach.
meals.dinner: Buzz's Original Steakhouse (Kailua, 10 min drive) — a beloved local institution with premium steaks, fresh catch, and a warm, family-welcoming atmosphere. Reserve the private lanai table.

day_by_day.notes: Lanikai Beach has limited parking; arrange hotel transportation. The Mokulua Islands kayak tour should be pre-booked and is weather-dependent. August is generally excellent for ocean conditions in East Oahu.

day_by_day.morning: Waimea Valley Botanical Garden and Waterfall Hike on the North Shore (approximately 1 hour from the hotel). Join a private guided family walk through 1,800 acres of lush tropical botanical gardens featuring over 5,000 plant species. The trail culminates at the stunning 45-foot Waimea Falls — a magical experience for children and adults alike. Swimming at the base of the falls is permitted (life jackets provided).
day_by_day.afternoon: After the hike, head to nearby Haleiwa Town on the North Shore for a leisurely afternoon. Explore the charming surf town's boutique shops and art galleries. Stop at the famous Matsumoto Shave Ice for a quintessential Hawaii treat.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset dinner at a North Shore restaurant before the scenic drive back to the hotel.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at the hotel before departure — avocado toast with poached eggs, fresh fruit, and Kona coffee to fuel the morning hike.
meals.lunch: Al fresco lunch at Waimea Valley's on-site café following the waterfall hike — fresh salads, sandwiches, and tropical drinks in the garden setting.
meals.dinner: Haleiwa Joe's Haiku Gardens (on the return route, Kaneohe) — a stunning open-air restaurant set in a botanical garden with exceptional seafood, prime rib, and one of Oahu's most romantic settings.

day_by_day.notes: Wear water shoes for the Waimea Falls swim. Book the private guided tour through the concierge for an enhanced botanical experience. The North Shore drive via Kamehameha Highway is scenic — allow extra time to stop at lookout points.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Maui via inter-island flight (Hawaiian Airlines or Mokulele Airlines, ~30 min). Upon arrival at Kahului Airport, a private luxury vehicle transfer takes the family to the iconic Kaanapali Beach on West Maui. Begin the morning with a guided outrigger canoe experience — a traditional Hawaiian paddling session on the calm waters off Kaanapali.
day_by_day.afternoon: Kaanapali Beach Family Day — one of Hawaii's most celebrated family-friendly beaches. Build sandcastles, snorkel the famous Black Rock (Puu Kekaa) where cliff diving ceremonies take place, and enjoy premium beach cabana service with attentive staff, chilled towels, and refreshments. Arrange a private surfing lesson for the kids through the beach concierge.
day_by_day.evening: Witness the legendary Cliff Diving Ceremony at Black Rock at sunset — a nightly tradition where a torch lighter dives from the lava rock into the sea. Dinner at a top Maui restaurant before the return flight to Oahu.

meals.breakfast: Light breakfast at the hotel before early departure — grab-and-go premium pastry boxes and Kona coffee prepared by the hotel.
meals.lunch: Beachside lunch at Japengo at Hyatt Regency Maui — upscale Pacific Rim cuisine with ocean views, featuring fresh sashimi, lobster bisque, and tropical cocktails.
meals.dinner: Mama's Fish House (Paia, East Maui) — one of Hawaii's most iconic and celebrated fine dining restaurants, featuring the freshest fish caught daily by local fishermen. Reservations are essential and should be booked months in advance.

day_by_day.notes: Book inter-island flights and Mama's Fish House reservations well in advance — Mama's is notoriously difficult to get into during peak season. Consider chartering a small private plane for the inter-island transfer for an ultra-luxury experience. Return flight to Oahu should be booked for 8:00–9:00 PM.

day_by_day.morning: Rest and recovery morning at the hotel. Enjoy a late, leisurely breakfast followed by a private in-suite spa experience — arrange through the hotel concierge for a couples' massage or family wellness session with a visiting therapist. Children can enjoy a supervised kids' activity program.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit Diamond Head State Monument (20 min from hotel) — hike the iconic 1.6-mile round-trip trail inside the volcanic crater for panoramic views of Waikiki and the Pacific Ocean. The hike takes approximately 1.5 hours and is suitable for older children. Alternatively, arrange a private helicopter tour over Diamond Head and the Oahu coastline for a more luxurious perspective.
day_by_day.evening: Explore Honolulu's vibrant Kakaako arts district, then enjoy a premium dinner in the city.

meals.breakfast: Indulgent in-suite breakfast — eggs cooked to order, Belgian waffles with fresh mango compote, smoked salmon platters, and a full Kona coffee and tea service.
meals.lunch: Post-hike lunch at Waioli Kitchen & Bake Shop (Manoa Valley) — a charming farm-to-table café known for its fresh, local ingredients and beautiful garden setting.
meals.dinner: MW Restaurant (Honolulu) — a celebrated Hawaii Regional Cuisine restaurant by James Beard Award-winning chefs Michelle Karr-Ueoka and Wade Ueoka, offering a stunning tasting menu highlighting local ingredients.

day_by_day.notes: Diamond Head requires advance online reservations for parking and entry. For families with younger children, the helicopter tour is a more comfortable and equally spectacular alternative to the hike. Book the helicopter tour through Blue Hawaiian Helicopters for the premium experience.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to the Big Island to explore Hawaii Volcanoes National Park. Depart early via inter-island flight to Hilo (approximately 45 min). A private luxury SUV and knowledgeable local guide meet you at the airport. Begin exploration of the park with a visit to the Kilauea Visitor Center, then walk the Kilauea Iki Trail through a hardened lava lake — a truly otherworldly family experience.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue exploring the park — visit the Thurston Lava Tube (a magnificent natural tunnel through ancient lava), the Chain of Craters Road with its dramatic coastal lava fields, and the Holei Sea Arch. The guide will provide expert geological and cultural context throughout. If volcanic activity permits, observe active lava flows or steam vents.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Hilo for dinner before the evening flight back to Oahu. Alternatively, consider an overnight stay at Volcano House (the historic hotel perched on the rim of Kilauea caldera) for a truly unique experience — subject to availability.

meals.breakfast: Early hotel breakfast before departure — quick but substantial: eggs, toast, fresh fruit, and coffee.
meals.lunch: Picnic lunch prepared by the hotel and enjoyed inside the national park at a scenic overlook — gourmet sandwiches, local chips, fresh fruit, and sparkling water.
meals.dinner: Hilo Bay Café (Hilo) — a beloved farm-to-table restaurant showcasing Big Island produce, fresh catch, and local flavors before the return flight.

day_by_day.notes: Hawaii Volcanoes National Park requires a vehicle entry fee (included in private tour package). Volcanic activity levels vary — check the USGS Hawaiian Volcano Observatory website before the trip. Bring layers as the park sits at elevation and can be significantly cooler. Sturdy closed-toe shoes are essential for lava field walking.

day_by_day.morning: Private sunrise kayaking or stand-up paddleboarding session at Kailua Bay — one of Oahu's most beautiful and calm bays, just 10 minutes from the hotel. A private instructor guides the family on the water as the sun rises over the Koolau Mountains. Afterward, explore the charming Kailua town with its boutique shops and local bakeries.
day_by_day.afternoon: Premium cultural experience: Private Hawaiian cultural workshop at the hotel or a nearby cultural center. Learn traditional Hawaiian arts such as lei making, hula dancing basics, and ukulele playing — a wonderful hands-on family activity. Follow with a relaxed afternoon at the hotel pool.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell-eve celebration dinner at one of Oahu's finest restaurants, toasting an unforgettable trip.

meals.breakfast: Post-kayaking breakfast at Cinnamon's Restaurant (Kailua) — famous for its red velvet pancakes, guava chiffon pancakes, and hearty local-style breakfasts. A beloved Kailua institution.
meals.lunch: Light poolside lunch at the hotel — fresh poke bowls, tropical salads, and fresh coconut water.
meals.dinner: La Mer at Halekulani (Waikiki, ~20 min drive) — Oahu's most acclaimed fine dining restaurant, offering French-inspired cuisine with Hawaiian influences in an elegant beachfront setting. The pinnacle of luxury dining on Oahu.

day_by_day.notes: La Mer requires formal attire and advance reservations — book as early as possible. The cultural workshop can be arranged through the hotel concierge and customized for the family's age group and interests. This is an ideal day for souvenir shopping in Kailua — far more authentic and less touristy than Waikiki.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Hawaii — enjoy one last sunrise walk along the Hanauma Bay shoreline. Take in the beauty of the volcanic crater bay that has been your home base for the trip. Pack and check out of the hotel with a late checkout arranged through the concierge (typically available until 1:00–2:00 PM at luxury properties).
day_by_day.afternoon: Depending on departure flight time, enjoy a final activity: visit the USS Arizona Memorial at Pearl Harbor (historically significant, approximately 30 min from the hotel) or spend the remaining hours at Waikiki Beach for a last swim and souvenir shopping on Kalakaua Avenue. Private luxury transfer to Honolulu International Airport.
day_by_day.evening: Depart Hawaii with incredible memories of a world-class family luxury vacation. Airport lounge access arranged through the concierge for a comfortable pre-flight experience.

meals.breakfast: Final hotel breakfast — a grand farewell spread: full Hawaiian breakfast with kalua pork hash, taro pancakes, fresh pineapple, papaya, and Kona coffee. Savor every last bite.
meals.lunch: Farewell lunch at Duke's Waikiki (if time permits before departure) — a legendary beachfront restaurant named after Duke Kahanamoku, serving fresh fish tacos, burgers, and tropical cocktails with an unbeatable ocean view.
meals.dinner: In-flight dining or airport lounge dining depending on departure time.

day_by_day.notes: Arrange all airport transfers and luggage handling through the hotel concierge the night before. Pearl Harbor requires advance timed-entry reservations. If the departure flight is early, skip Pearl Harbor and opt for a final relaxed beach morning. Ensure all duty-free purchases and Hawaiian food gifts (Kona coffee, macadamia nuts, local chocolates) are packed in checked luggage per TSA guidelines.
